purpose: A dated, evidence-bounded review of inputs that might keep metric-v3 development moving after NLM confirmed that previous annual PubMed baselines are not available. This contract does not weaken or replace the original historical-record readiness gate.

decision_rule.original_gate: Only complete, checksummed releases matching the four pinned NLM inventories can satisfy the existing historical-baseline contract.
decision_rule.redesign_gate: A secondary dated snapshot may support a separately pre-registered experiment only after its payload, fixed corpus scope, citation-to-MeSH fields, version date, and limitations are measured and pinned.
decision_rule.current_or_title_abstract_only_data: Current maintained indexing and snapshots without historical MeSH assignments remain engineering or metadata aids only.

evidence.label: BioASQ dataset catalog: versioned MeSH assignments, v2013 counts, registered access, and CC BY 2.5 terms
BioASQ public Task 1a sample used for the bounded field-semantics audit
Peer-reviewed BioASQ overview: all MEDLINE articles with title, abstract, and MeSH labels indexed before 1 March 2013
BioASQ challenge report: v2013 is a 10,876,004-article MEDLINE collection published after 1949
BioASQ announcement dating initial Task 1a training-data availability to 18 March 2013

alternatives.potential_role: A separately pre-registered 2013-snapshot pilot over the corpus BioASQ actually contains, after acquisition and audit. It may support post-snapshot discovery cases but is not an NLM baseline substitute.
blockers: The registered-download payload has not been acquired, checksummed, or parsed in this repository.
The official descriptions define a post-1949 MEDLINE article corpus rather than the complete 21,508,439-record 2013 NLM baseline; the two published counts are not a measured coverage fraction.

The official five-record sample is consistent with meshMajor containing all assigned descriptors rather than only major-topic headings. A 416-record, hash-selected, year-stratified semantics protocol is frozen before full-payload access, but it cannot run until the registered corpus is acquired.
Only a 2013 snapshot is relevant here, so it cannot supply the missing 2007, 2011, and 2012 releases.
Using it changes the experimental population and therefore requires a new pre-registration rather than a source-status flip.
alternatives.next_action: Activate a BioASQ account, expose its credentials only as BIOASQ_USERNAME and BIOASQ_PASSWORD, run pipeline.benchmark.bioasq_download full, then run pipeline.benchmark.bioasq_snapshot with --require-declared-match and pipeline.benchmark.bioasq_semantics under the checksum-pinned protocol. Commit only generated manifests and bounded audit records, not credentials or the multi-gigabyte payload.
